source_refs.note: Transverse and Longitudinal Waves: a main subheading of 7.1 Waves, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 139-141.

blocks.text: There are two main types of waves which are named as transverse waves and longitudinal waves. A transverse wave is one in which the vibrations of the particles are at right angle to the direction in which the energy of the wave is travelling. Whereas a longitudinal wave is one in which the direction of the vibration of the particles is along or parallel to the the direction in which the energy of the wave is travelling.

blocks.alt: (a) Transverse waves: a hand on the left moves a long spring lying on a table sideways (up-down arrows on the handle); the spring forms a wave that travels right, arrow labelled Wave, to the Fixed end. (b) Longitudinal waves: the hand pushes and pulls the spring along its length (left-right arrows); compressions and stretched parts move along it to the Fixed end.
